title: John Glenn Wouldn't Fly Without Her

brand.cta: Follow The Black History Room for one story a day.

beats.text: John Glenn wouldn't fly without her.
Born in West Virginia in 1918, she finished college at eighteen, with top honors in math and French.
In 1953, Langley hired her as a human computer, in a segregated unit of Black women.
In 1961, she calculated the flight path of the first American in space, Alan Shepard.
In 1962, John Glenn was about to orbit the Earth. The new electronic computers had done the math.
Glenn didn't trust them. Get the girl, he said, to check the numbers. If she says they're good, I'm ready to go.
She checked them by hand. And he flew.
She went on to help calculate the path to the Moon for Apollo 11.
She retired in 1986, after 33 years and 26 research reports.
In 2015, at 97, she received the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
She died in 2020, at 101. The man who orbited the Earth trusted her more than the machine.

facts.claim: Glenn asked for Johnson to check the computer's orbital numbers by hand before Friendship 7; 'If she says they're good, then I'm ready to go.'
Born 1918, White Sulphur Springs, W.Va.; graduated 1937 at 18, summa cum laude, B.S. mathematics and French.
Joined NACA Langley in 1953 in the all-Black West Area Computing section (Hampton, Virginia).
Trajectory analysis for Shepard's Freedom 7, May 1961, America's first human spaceflight.
Friendship 7 launched 20 Feb 1962; the orbital numbers had been computed by NASA's electronic computers.
Helped calculate the Apollo 11 trajectory (1969 Moon landing).
Retired 1986 after 33 years; authored or co-authored 26 research reports.
Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Obama, 24 Nov 2015, aged 97.
